messages:
Ellie T: dropped a micro-prototype for a regression diff timeline compact view: https://figma.com/file/pqr555. goal: make long diff runs scannable without losing approval CTA prominence. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Ravi S: quick look 1: nice reduced density. one worry: the approve/reject buttons get hidden under a 'more' menu when screen width is small. that makes the primary action less discoverable.
Noah M: agreed. primary CTA should never be nested. maybe show a single prominent CTA (Approve) and move secondary actions into the overflow. keep keyboard shortcut visible in the tooltip.
Ellie T: good call. idea: always show the primary CTA and an active-state badge for the current selected result. overflow menu contains 'Request changes' and 'Add note'. on collapse, show a compact label like "1/8 diffs" plus the primary CTA.
Ravi S: accessibility: when we hide actions into overflow, the menu must be reachable by keyboard and announced by SRs. add aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the overflow button, and a visible focus ring.
Noah M: also recommend a live region when a diff is approved via keyboard or shortcut: "Diff 3 approved." keeps screen reader users informed. lightweight rule: any destructive/approval action should trigger polite aria-live updates.
accessibility-bot: Accessibility checklist updated: regression-compact -> primary-cta-visible, overflow-has-aria, focus-visible, aria-live-on-action. See /docs/accessibility/regression-compact.md :white_check_mark:
Ellie T: perfect. I'll update the prototype to always show primary CTA and add aria attributes + live announce. follow-ups: @Ravi S to prototype overflow keyboard behavior; @Noah M to add aria-live test cases. target: flag rollout in two sprints. :rocket:
